dc01.title: Like button
dc01.summary: A photo post card is built. Make the heart toggle, fill red, and keep the like count in sync.
dc01.brief:
A small photo-sharing app, lumen. App.tsx has TopBar, PostCard, PostHeader, PostPhoto and a static LikeButton. No API: the post is a constant.

Read components/Icons.tsx and utils/format.ts first. The heart icon (it takes a filled prop) and the "241 likes" text helper already exist and are worth reusing.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The heart, the likes line and (later) the photo all depend on liked, so the state goes in PostCard, the closest common parent. LikeButton gets liked and onToggle as props and stays dumb. The count is post.likes + 1 when liked. I won't store the count, I'll derive it."
requirements: Clicking the heart toggles liked. Liked: the heart is filled (<HeartIcon filled />) and red (add is-liked to the button). Clicking again unlikes it (outline, dark)
The likes line reads "241 likes", and "242 likes" while liked. The count is derived from post.likes, not kept in its own state
The button's aria-label is "Like" / "Unlike" and it has aria-pressed (true while liked). The CSS "pop" then plays on its own when liked

change.title: Double-click to like
change.html:
"Everyone double-taps the photo. Make that work."

  • Double-clicking the photo likes the post.
  • If it is already liked, double-clicking keeps it liked (it never unlikes).

Hint: PostPhoto needs an onDoubleClick prop. The state is already in the right place.

hints: State placement: who needs to know about liked? The button and the likes line. Put it in their parent, PostCard.
HeartIcon already takes a filled prop. Color comes from currentColor, so a CSS class that sets color turns it red.
Toggle with the updater form: setLiked((prev) => { return !prev; });
Derive the number above the return: let likeCount = post.likes; if (liked) { likeCount = post.likes + 1; } then pluralize(likeCount, "like").
For the pop, search: mdn css @keyframes. Scale 1 → 1.25 → 1 over 0.25s.
rubric: State lives in PostCard, not in LikeButton
LikeButton takes liked + onToggle props
Count is derived, not a second piece of state
Updater form used for the toggle
Reused HeartIcon and pluralize
Double-click only sets liked to true
Class names and labels decided above the return

primitives.name: useState updater form
primitives.example: setLiked((prev) => { return !prev; });   // false -> true -> false
primitives.note: Pass a function when the new state depends on the old one. React calls it with the latest value, so quick double clicks never read a stale value. Returns nothing; it schedules a re-render.

primitives.name: Callback prop types
primitives.syntax: type Props = { liked: boolean; onToggle: () => void; }
primitives.example:
function LikeButton({ liked, onToggle }: Props) { … }
<LikeButton liked={liked} onToggle={handleToggle} />
primitives.note: () => void means "a function that takes nothing and returns nothing". With an argument: (id: string) => void. Pass the function itself, not handleToggle().

primitives.name: onDoubleClick
primitives.example: <div className="photo" onDoubleClick={() => { onDoubleClick(); }} />
primitives.note: Fires after two quick clicks on the same element (each click also fires onClick first). Works on any element, not just buttons.

dc02.title: Bio character counter
dc02.summary: A dev-profile settings page. Add a live "characters left" counter with warning and over-limit states.
dc02.brief:
Settings page of a developer platform, forge. ProfileForm already holds bio in state (a controlled textarea) and saves on click. BIO_LIMIT is 160. No API.

Read components/Field.tsx: the counter goes inside the Bio Field, under the textarea.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"bio is already state, so everything new is derived from bio.length: remaining, the text and (later) the status. Nothing new goes in state. I'll pull it into a small BioMeter component that takes the length, and compute isOver in the form for the Save button."
requirements: Under the bio, right-aligned and monospace (.bio-meter > .bio-count): "96 characters left", updating as you type. Exactly 1 reads "1 character left". Over the limit it reads "5 characters over" (never a negative number)
Save profile is disabled while the bio is over 160 characters
Under 20 left the counter turns amber (is-warn on .bio-meter). Over the limit it turns red (is-over)
While over, the textarea border turns red too (is-over on the textarea)

change.title: Progress bar
change.html:
"Design wants a visual for this."

  • Add a thin bar (4px, pill) to the left of the counter, filling from 0% to 100% as the bio approaches 160 (capped at 100%).
  • It uses the same color rules: primary, then amber under 20 left, red when over.

Hint: an inline style object built above the return: const fillStyle = { width: percent + "%" };

hints: You need no new state. const remaining = BIO_LIMIT - bio.length;
Text with an if / else if chain above the return. For "over", flip the sign: -remaining + " characters over" (or Math.abs(remaining)). Search: mdn Math.abs.
Disable with disabled={isOver}, where const isOver = bio.length > BIO_LIMIT;. .btn-primary:disabled is already styled.
Next: decide one status string above the return ("ok", "warn", "over") and use it for the class: "bio-meter is-" + status. One decision, used everywhere.
Change: search mdn Math.min. const percent = Math.min(100, (length / BIO_LIMIT) * 100); then style={{ width: percent + "%" }} (build the object above the return).
rubric: No new state: all derived from bio.length
Singular / plural and "over" wording correct
Save disabled exactly when over
Counter placed inside the existing Field
Status decided once, reused for colour classes
Bar width capped at 100%

primitives.name: Template literals
primitives.example:
const n = 96;
`${n} characters left`   // "96 characters left"
primitives.note: Backticks, not quotes. Anything inside ${ } is evaluated and turned into text. Same result as n + " characters left", easier to read.

primitives.name: Math.abs()
primitives.example:
Math.abs(-5)   // 5
Math.abs(5)    // 5
primitives.note: Returns the number without its sign. Handy for "5 characters over" when remaining is -5. -remaining works too.

primitives.name: Math.min() as a cap
primitives.note: Returns the smallest argument, so it caps a value at a maximum. (Math.max does the opposite: a floor.)

primitives.name: style prop (inline style object)
primitives.example:
const fillStyle = { width: 50 + "%" };
<div className="fill" style={fillStyle} />   // width: 50%
primitives.note: React takes an object, not a CSS string. Property names are camelCase (backgroundColor). Use it only for values computed at runtime; everything else stays in CSS classes.

dc03.title: Password show/hide + strength
dc03.summary: A bank sign-up form. Add a Show/Hide toggle and a Weak / Fair / Strong label derived from three password rules.
dc03.brief:
The account sign-up form for Ledgerly, a business bank. SignUpForm already holds email and password as controlled inputs. The password input sits in an empty .password-wrap (already position: relative). No API.

The strength rules: 8+ characters, contains a number, contains a symbol (anything not a letter or digit). Count the rules met: 0–1 → Weak, 2 → Fair, 3 → Strong.

The CSS is already written (bottom of styles.css, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE): today is about React, not stylesheets. Use .show-btn, .strength + .strength-label, and later .segments / .segment and .rules / .rule.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working (Show/Hide + the text label). Strong: plus 3–4 (bars + disabled button).
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Only one new piece of state: showPassword. Everything about strength is derived from password on each render: three true/false checks (two of them with RegExp.test), count how many are true, and look the word up in ['Weak', 'Weak', 'Fair', 'Strong']. Empty password means no label. The input's type and the button text are decided above the return. The button needs type=\"button\" or it submits the form."
requirements: A Show text button inside the right edge of the password field (.show-btn) switches the input to plain text and its label to Hide. Clicking again hides it. It must not submit the form

Under the password, right-aligned, a text label (<div class="strength"><span class="strength-label">) from the three rules: 0 or 1 met → Weak, 2 → Fair, 3 → Strong. Empty password: no label. "abc" → Weak, "abcdefgh1" → Fair, "abcdefgh1!" → Strong

3 bar segments to the left of the label. Lit segments = 1 / 2 / 3 for Weak / Fair / Strong (grey when empty), coloured red / amber / green, and the label takes the same colour (put is-weak / is-fair / is-strong on .strength, is-on on lit segments)
Create account is disabled until the email contains "@" and the password is Strong

change.title: Show the rules
change.html:
"Users don't know what makes it Strong."

  • Under the meter, list the three rules: "At least 8 characters", "Contains a number", "Contains a symbol".
  • Unmet: muted with ○. Met: green with ✓ (.rule / .rule.is-met, .rule-mark are styled). Updates as you type.

Hint: if your rules are an array of { id, label, met }, this is one .map.

hints: The toggle is type={inputType} where inputType is "password" or "text", decided above the return with an if.
A <button> inside a <form> submits it by default. Give it type="button". Search: mdn button type attribute.
Test a string with a regex: /\d/.test(password) is true when it contains a digit; /[^A-Za-z0-9]/.test(password) when it contains a symbol. Search: mdn RegExp test.
Count with an array: const rules = [{ id: "length", label: "At least 8 characters", met: password.length >= 8 }, …]; then const score = rules.filter((r) => { return r.met; }).length;

Word from the score: const LEVELS = ["Weak", "Weak", "Fair", "Strong"]; then let strength = ""; if (password !== "") { strength = LEVELS[score]; } and render <span className="strength-label">{strength}</span>.

Next: segments are [1, 2, 3].map((n) => { … }) with is-on when n <= level (level = Math.max(score, 1) when typed), and one class on .strength ("strength is-" + strength.toLowerCase()) colours everything.
rubric: Only showPassword is new state; strength is derived
Toggle button is type="button" (and labelled)
Regex checks use .test, not manual loops
Empty vs typed handled (no label when empty, Weak when typed)
Score → word via a lookup, decided above the return
Segments built with map, coloured by one wrapper class
Submit gate reuses the same derived strength

primitives.name: RegExp.test()
primitives.example:
/\d/.test('abc1')   // true  (contains a digit)
/\d/.test('abc')    // false
primitives.note: Returns true/false: does the string contain a match anywhere? Perfect for simple checks like "has a number". Write the regex between slashes, no quotes.

primitives.name: Character classes: \d and [^...]
primitives.example:
/[^A-Za-z0-9]/.test('pass!')   // true  ('!' is not a letter or digit)
/[A-Z]/.test('pass')          // false
primitives.note: \d = any digit. [abc] = any one of these. [^abc] = any character except these (the ^ inside brackets means NOT). So [^A-Za-z0-9] = a symbol or space.

primitives.name: Count matches: filter().length
primitives.example: [true, false, true].filter((ok) => { return ok; }).length   // 2
primitives.note: filter returns a new array of the items where the callback returned true; .length of that is the count. The original array is not changed.

primitives.name: <button type="button">
primitives.note: A button inside a form defaults to type="submit". Any button that is not the submit button needs type="button". Same idea: <input type={inputType}> switches between "password" and "text".

dc04.title: Product page tabs
dc04.summary: A coffee-gear product page. Turn the details section into Description / Specs / Reviews tabs.
dc04.brief:
A product page for Kettle & Co. ProductPage already loads the product from api.ts (getProduct waits 0.4–1.2 s) and shows "Loading product…" first. Below the summary it only shows the description.

Read components/Panels.tsx: DescriptionPanel, SpecsTable and ReviewList are already built. Your job is the tab bar that switches between them.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"One piece of state: which tab is active, as an id string, default "description". I'll make a ProductTabs component with an array of { id, label } and map it to buttons. The panel is chosen above the return with an if/else. If anything outside the tabs ever needs to switch tab, the state moves up to ProductPage."
requirements: A tab bar (.tabs of <button class="tab">) with Description, Specs and Reviews (3) (the count comes from the data). Description is active on load
Clicking a tab shows only that panel (reuse the three panel components). The active tab gets is-active (dark, weight 600, 2px --accent underline: already in the CSS)
Tab semantics: the bar has role="tablist", each tab has role="tab" and aria-selected, the panel wrapper has role="tabpanel"

change.title: Rating link jumps to reviews
change.html:
"People click the star rating expecting reviews."

  • Make "★ 4.7 · 3 reviews" in the summary a link-style button (underlined).
  • Clicking it switches the tabs to Reviews.

Hint: ProductSummary and the tabs are siblings. Where must activeTab live now?

hints: State: const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState<TabId>("description"); with type TabId = "description" | "specs" | "reviews";
Labels as data: const tabs = [{ id: "description", label: "Description" }, …, { id: "reviews", label: "Reviews (" + product.reviews.length + ")" }]; then tabs.map(...) to buttons.
Choose the panel above the return: let panel = <DescriptionPanel ... />; if (activeTab === "specs") { panel = ...; } else if ...
Change: lift activeTab to ProductPage and pass activeTab + onChange down to the tabs, and an onReviewsClick to the summary. Search: react lifting state up.
rubric: Active tab stored as an id, not three booleans
Tabs rendered from an array with map
Panel chosen above the return
Reused the existing panel components
Review count derived from data
Lifted state cleanly for the change
Tab semantics (role, aria-selected)

primitives.name: String literal union type
primitives.example:
let t: TabId = 'specs';    // ok
t = 'photos';              // error: not one of the three
primitives.note: A type that only allows these exact strings. Catches typos at compile time and documents every option in one line.

primitives.name: useState<Type>(initial)
primitives.example:
const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState<TabId>('description');
setActiveTab('reviews');   // ok
primitives.note: The <Type> tells TypeScript what the state may hold when it can't guess from the initial value (unions, null, empty arrays).

primitives.name: Array.map() to elements, with key
primitives.example:
[{ id: 'a', label: 'A' }].map((t) => { return <button key={t.id}>{t.label}</button>; })
// [<button>A</button>]
primitives.note: Returns a new array of elements React can render. Each needs a stable, unique key (an id, not the index).

primitives.name: Passing a setter down
primitives.example: function ProductTabs({ onChange }: { onChange: (t: TabId) => void }) { … onChange('specs'); }
primitives.note: When two siblings need the same state, put it in their parent and pass the value and a callback down. A setter is just a function, so it can be the callback.

dc05.title: FAQ accordion
dc05.summary: A hosting pricing page. Make the FAQ an accordion: one item open at a time, click again to close.
dc05.brief:
The pricing page for Skyport, a deploy platform. FaqSection maps FAQS (in data/faqs.ts) to FaqItems. Each question is already a button with a ChevronIcon (points down). Nothing opens yet. No API.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3 (Stretch 4 is optional).
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"One item open at a time means the state is a single openId (string or null) in FaqSection, not a boolean in each item. Each FaqItem gets isOpen and onToggle(id). Toggle: if the clicked id is already open, set null, otherwise set it. The chevron rotation is already CSS on an is-open class."
requirements: Clicking a question shows its answer below it (<div class="faq-answer"><p>…). Opening another question closes the one that was open
Clicking the open question closes it. The open item has is-open on its <li> (the CSS then rotates the chevron and highlights it)
The question button has aria-expanded (true while open)

Under each open answer: "Was this helpful?" with Yes / No pill buttons (.feedback, .vote-btn). After a vote they are replaced by "Thanks for the feedback!" (.thanks) for that question, and it stays that way after closing and reopening it

change.title: Collapse button
change.html:
"On mobile, people can't find how to close an answer."

  • Put the FAQ title in a .faq-head row with a Collapse link-button (.collapse-btn) on the right.
  • It only shows while a question is open, and clicking it closes it.

Hint: openId already lives in FaqSection, the same component as the title.

hints: const [openId, setOpenId] = useState<string | null>(null); in FaqSection.
Toggle: setOpenId((prev) => { if (prev === id) { return null; } return id; });
In the map: const isOpen = faq.id === openId; then pass isOpen and onToggle down. In the item: let answer = null; if (isOpen) { answer = <div className="faq-answer">…</div>; }
Change: let collapseBtn = null; if (openId !== null) { collapseBtn = <button …>Collapse</button>; }
Stretch: setVotes((prev) => { return { ...prev, [id]: vote }; }); Search: mdn computed property names for [id].
rubric: Single openId instead of per-item booleans
Clicking the open item closes it
Items are dumb: isOpen + onToggle props
Answer and class decided above the return
Collapse reuses the same state (no new state)
aria-expanded on the button
Votes keyed by id, immutable update (stretch)

primitives.name: Nullable state: string | null
primitives.note: null means "nothing selected". Without the <string | null>, TypeScript infers the type null only and rejects "q2".

primitives.name: Updater with a condition
primitives.syntax: setX((prev) => { if (prev === id) { return null; } return id; })
primitives.example:
// prev 'q2', click 'q2' -> null (closes)
// prev 'q2', click 'q4' -> 'q4'
primitives.note: An updater can contain any logic, as long as it returns the next value. This one makes "click again to close" a single function.

primitives.name: null renders nothing
primitives.example:
{null}        // renders nothing
{answer}      // renders the div when it was set
primitives.note: React skips null, undefined and false. Deciding into a variable above the return keeps JSX free of && and ternaries.

dc06.title: Study planner todos
dc06.summary: A student weekly planner. Wire up adding and completing tasks with immutable array updates.
dc06.brief:
A weekly planner, studyhall. Planner already loads tasks from api.ts (getTasks waits 0.5–1.2 s) with a loading state, and renders TaskRows. TaskRow is already wired: it calls onToggle(id) / onDelete(id) and shows is-done, but the two handlers in Planner are empty. The add input is not wired at all.

Read utils/id.ts: new tasks need ids.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4 (Stretch 5 is optional).
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The list lives in Planner (it's already there). AddTask owns only its draft text and calls onAdd(title). Every update uses the updater form and returns a new array: spread to add, map + object spread to toggle, filter to delete. The 'left' count is derived with filter."
requirements: Typing a title and pressing Enter or clicking Add adds it to the bottom of the list (not done, subject "Inbox", id from makeId("t")) and clears the input. Blank / spaces-only input adds nothing
Clicking a checkbox toggles that task (fill in handleToggle): done tasks are struck through and muted. Update immutably
The × button deletes that task (fill in handleDelete), and Add is disabled while the input is blank
The header shows a yellow pill "3 left" (.left-badge, count of not-done tasks), updating live; "All done" (is-done, green) at 0. Nothing shows while loading
Below the list, a right-aligned Clear completed (2) button (.planner-foot > .clear-btn) with the number of done tasks. It only appears when at least one task is done, and removes all done tasks

change.title: Newest first
change.html:
"Students add the urgent thing last, then can't find it."

  • New tasks now go to the top of the list instead of the bottom.

Hint: it's the order inside one spread.

hints: Wrap the input and button in a <form onSubmit> and you get Enter for free. Call e.preventDefault(). Search: mdn submit event preventDefault.
AddTask keeps draft state and calls onAdd(draft.trim()); the list is updated in Planner: setTasks((prev) => { return [...prev, task]; }); with id: makeId("t").
Toggle: prev.map((t) => { if (t.id !== id) { return t; } return { ...t, done: !t.done }; }). Never set t.done directly.
Delete / clear: prev.filter(...). Count: tasks.filter((t) => { return !t.done; }).length.
Change: [task, ...prev] puts it first.
rubric: List state stays in Planner; AddTask owns only the draft
Form submit with preventDefault (Enter works)
Trimmed empty input ignored
map / filter / spread, no mutation
Reused makeId
Count derived, not stored
Clear completed only renders when needed (stretch)

primitives.name: Form submit + e.preventDefault()
primitives.note: A form fires submit on Enter in any input and on its submit button, so one handler covers both. Without preventDefault() the browser reloads the page.

primitives.name: String.trim()
primitives.example:
'  Lab report  '.trim()   // 'Lab report'
'   '.trim() === ''         // true
primitives.note: Returns a new string without spaces at both ends. The usual way to ignore blank input.

primitives.name: Spread to add: [...arr, x]
primitives.note: Builds a new array. Never push into state: React compares by reference and would not see the change.

primitives.name: Object spread to update one field
primitives.example:
const t = { id: 't1', done: false };
{ ...t, done: !t.done }   // { id: 't1', done: true }  (t unchanged)
primitives.note: Copies every property, then overrides the ones after it. Use it inside .map to change one item immutably.

dc07.title: Searchable staff directory
dc07.summary: A hospital care-team directory. Load staff from a slow API, then filter by name or role as you type.
dc07.brief:
The staff directory for Cedar Health. The page, toolbar and search box exist, and StaffCard (in components/) renders one person. But staff is an empty array: you load it.

Read api.ts first. getStaff() returns a Promise and takes a random 0.4–1.3 s, so you need useEffect + .then.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4 (Stretch 5 is optional).
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"State in Directory: staff and query (and loading for Next). Load once in a useEffect with a cancelled guard. The visible list is derived: lowercase the trimmed query and keep people whose name or role includes it. Later, one if/else chain above the return for loading / no matches / list."
requirements: On mount, load the list with getStaff() inside a useEffect (with a cancelled guard) and render it with the existing StaffCards
The search input is controlled and filters by name or role, case-insensitive, ignoring surrounding spaces ("nurse" finds both nurses, " PRIYA " finds Dr. Priya Nair)
Show "Loading care team…" (in a .message) until the data arrives, then above the list: "Showing 2 of 9" (.count)
When nothing matches: No matches for “xyz”. and a Clear search link-button (.link-btn) that empties the input
An On call now pill button (.chip) to the right of the search. When on (is-on, aria-pressed), only on-call staff show. It combines with the search, and the count stays right

change.title: Search departments too
change.html:
"Nurses type the ward, not the job title."

  • The search also matches the person's department: "pediatrics" now finds Dr. Sofia Marquez and Ethan Brooks.
  • Update the placeholder to "Search name, role or department".

Hint: one more || in the same filter.

hints: Copy the loading shape: useEffect(() => { let cancelled = false; getStaff().then((data) => { if (cancelled) { return; } setStaff(data); }); return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, []);
Type the state: useState<Staff[]>([]), and import type { Staff } from "./api";
Normalize once above the filter: const q = query.trim().toLowerCase(); then person.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || person.role.toLowerCase().includes(q). Search: mdn String includes.
Next: decide the body above the return: let body; if (loading) { ... } else if (visible.length === 0) { ... } else { ... }
rubric: Loading pattern with a cancelled guard
Filtered list derived, not stored
Case-insensitive, trimmed match on several fields
Reused StaffCard
Loading, empty and list states all handled
Filters combine in one pass

primitives.name: useEffect + cleanup (load once)
primitives.note: [] = run once after the first render. The returned function runs on unmount; the cancelled flag stops a late response from setting state.

primitives.name: Promise.then()
primitives.example: getStaff().then((data) => { console.log(data.length); });   // 9 (after ~1s)
primitives.note: Runs the callback later, when the promise resolves, with its value. The line after .then(...) runs immediately, before the data arrives.

primitives.name: includes() + toLowerCase()
primitives.example:
'Charge Nurse'.toLowerCase().includes('nurse')   // true
'Charge Nurse'.includes('nurse')                 // false (case!)
primitives.note: includes returns true/false and is case-sensitive, so lowercase both sides. 'abc'.includes('') is true, so an empty search shows everyone.

primitives.name: Array.filter()
primitives.example:
[{ n: 'A', onCall: true }, { n: 'B', onCall: false }].filter((p) => { return p.onCall; })
// [{ n: 'A', onCall: true }]
primitives.note: Returns a new array with the items where the callback returned true. Derive it on each render; don't store the filtered list in state.

dc08.title: Ticket quantity stepper
dc08.summary: A concert checkout panel. Make the − / + stepper work between 1 and 8 and keep the totals right.
dc08.brief:
A ticket checkout for gigbox. TicketPanel shows the tier, a static stepper showing "1", a subtotal and Checkout. The event data is in data/event.ts. No API.

Read utils/money.ts: formatPrice(cents) already formats every price on the page. All prices are in cents.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3 (Stretch 4 is optional).
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"One number in state, qty, starting at 1 in TicketPanel. − and + use the updater form and clamp with Math.max / Math.min, so they can't go out of range even with fast clicks. The subtotal (and later atMin, atMax, fees) are all derived from qty."
requirements: − and + change the quantity by 1. It starts at 1, never goes below 1 or above 8
The subtotal row reads "Subtotal (3 × $48.00)" and $144.00, using formatPrice

− is disabled at 1 and + is disabled at 8 (faded: .step-btn:disabled is styled). At 8, an amber note under the stepper: "Max 8 tickets per order" (.max-note). The buttons have aria-labels "Decrease quantity" / "Increase quantity"
Under the subtotal, a muted Service fees row (.summary-row.is-muted, event.feeCents × quantity) and a bold Total row (.summary-row.is-total, subtotal + fees)

primitives.name: Clamp with Math.max / Math.min
primitives.example:
Math.min(8, 8 + 1)   // 8   (never above 8)
Math.max(1, 1 - 1)   // 1   (never below 1)
primitives.note: Math.min returns the smallest argument (a ceiling); Math.max the largest (a floor). Together they keep a number in range.

primitives.name: Number.toFixed()

dc09.title: Sort-by dropdown
dc09.summary: A vacation-stays listing. Build the "Sort by" dropdown menu, then make it re-sort the grid and close on outside click.
dc09.brief:
Search results for staybird. StaysPage already loads stays from api.ts (getStays waits 0.3–1.0 s, in "Recommended" order) and renders StayCards. It already holds sortKey and passes it to SortMenu as value + onChange, and SortMenu already shows the current label. But the button does nothing, and the grid ignores sortKey.

useRef and useEffect are already imported. You will need them for Next.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4 (Stretch 5 is optional).
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Two pieces of state in two places. sortKey is already in StaysPage because the grid needs it. open goes inside SortMenu because nobody else cares. Picking an option calls onChange(key) and closes. Sorting is a pure function that copies first, and Recommended returns the API order untouched. For outside click: a ref on the wrapper and a document mousedown listener only while open."
requirements: Clicking the button opens a menu below it, right-aligned (<ul class="sort-menu"> of <button class="sort-option">): Recommended, Price: low to high, Price: high to low, Top rated (from SORT_OPTIONS). Clicking the button again closes it
Choosing an option closes the menu and calls onChange, so the button shows it ("Sort by: Top rated")
The grid re-sorts by sortKey. Recommended restores the original API order. Do not mutate the loaded array
Clicking anywhere outside the menu closes it (the document listener is removed when it closes)
The selected option is highlighted (is-selected: --primary-soft, primary text) with a ✓ on the right (.check)

change.title: Escape closes it
change.html:
"QA filed a keyboard bug against the dropdown."

  • Pressing Escape closes the menu.

Hint: if you have the outside-click effect, it's a second listener in the same effect (and the same cleanup).

hints: const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); inside SortMenu. Build let menu = null; if (open) { menu = <ul className="sort-menu">…</ul>; } above the return and render {menu} after the button.
Select: function handleSelect(key: SortKey) { onChange(key); setOpen(false); }
Next: .sort() sorts in place. Copy first: const copy = [...stays]; copy.sort((a, b) => { return a.pricePerNight - b.pricePerNight; }); Search: mdn array sort compare function.

Outside click: const wrapRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null); on the wrapper, then in the listener if (wrapRef.current && !wrapRef.current.contains(e.target as Node)) { setOpen(false); }. Search: mdn Node contains.
Add the listeners in a useEffect that depends on [open], return early when closed, and remove them in the cleanup. Escape: if (e.key === "Escape") { setOpen(false); }
rubric: sortKey in the page, open in the menu
Menu built above the return, closes on select
Copied before sorting; recommended = original order
Sorted list derived, not stored
Outside click via ref.contains
Listeners cleaned up
Escape handled in the same effect

primitives.name: document.addEventListener + cleanup
primitives.note: For events outside your component (anywhere on the page). Remove with the same function in the effect cleanup, or listeners pile up on every open.

primitives.name: KeyboardEvent.key
primitives.example:
// pressing Esc  -> e.key is 'Escape'
// pressing Enter -> 'Enter',  arrow down -> 'ArrowDown'
primitives.note: A readable string for the key pressed. Use e.key, not the old keyCode numbers.

primitives.name: Copy, then sort
primitives.example:
[3, 1, 2].sort((a, b) => { return a - b; })   // [1, 2, 3]
// b - a for descending
primitives.note: sort mutates the array it is called on (and returns it). Copy state first with spread. The compare function returns negative (a first), positive (b first) or 0.

primitives.name: useRef + Node.contains()
primitives.note: Returns true if the node is the element itself or anywhere inside it. ref.current is null until mounted, so check it first.

dc10.title: Star rating input
dc10.summary: A food-delivery review form. Make the five stars clickable with a word label, then add a hover preview and Clear.
dc10.brief:
The "rate your order" screen of forkful. ReviewForm has the order summary, a comment box and Submit (which shows ThankYou). StarRating is five grey static stars. No API.

Read data/order.ts: LABELS maps a star count to a word.

The CSS for the new UI is already in styles.css (bottom block, marked CORE / NEXT / CHANGE). Today is about React: just use those class names.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4 (Stretch 5 is optional).
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The rating is submitted, so rating lives in ReviewForm and StarRating is controlled with value + onChange. Stars come from [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map, and star N is on when n <= value. The label is LABELS[value]. Later, hover is purely visual, so hover is local state in StarRating, and what I show is hover if hovering, otherwise value."
requirements: The five stars are <button class="star">s. Clicking star N sets the rating to N and fills stars 1..N gold (is-on). Under the stars, the label shows the word (Terrible / Poor / Okay / Good / Excellent), or muted "Tap a star to rate" when 0 (.rating-label, is-empty)
Submit review is disabled until a rating is set
Hovering star N previews it: stars 1..N fill and the label shows that word. Moving the mouse off the stars restores the saved rating
A Clear link-button (.clear-btn) appears under the label once rated and resets to 0. Each star has aria-label "Rate 3 out of 5"

When the rating is 1 or 2, show "What went wrong?" with pill chips (.chip): Late, Cold food, Missing item, Wrong order. Several can be on (is-on). With 1–2 stars, Submit stays disabled until at least one chip is on. At 3+ stars the chips disappear and are not required

change.title: Echo the rating
change.html:
"People aren't sure their rating went through."

  • The thank-you card shows a line above the paragraph: "You rated it ★★★★ Good" (one ★ per star, then the word), in .thanks-rating.

Hint: ThankYou is rendered by App, not by the form. How does the rating get there?

hints: Controlled component: function StarRating({ value, onChange }: { value: number; onChange: (n: number) => void }), with const [rating, setRating] = useState(0); in ReviewForm.

Stars: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((n) => { let cls = "star"; if (n <= value) { cls = "star is-on"; } return <button key={n} type="button" …>★</button>; }). Stars are buttons inside a form, so type="button" or they submit it.
Label: let label = "Tap a star to rate"; if (value > 0) { label = LABELS[value]; }. Submit: disabled={rating === 0}.
Next: let shown = value; if (hover > 0) { shown = hover; }. Use onMouseEnter on each star and one onMouseLeave on the row. Search: mdn mouseenter vs mouseover.
Change: give onSubmit an argument, (rating: number) => void, keep it in state in App, and pass it to ThankYou. Search: mdn string repeat for the stars.

Stars mapped from [1..5], not copy-pasted
type="button" on stars
Label from LABELS, decided above the return
Submit gate derived
Hover local to the stars, shown = hover or value
Rating passed up through the callback for the change

primitives.name: Look up by index: arr[n]
primitives.note: Arrays start at 0, so a dummy '' at index 0 lets the star count be the index. Out of range returns undefined, not an error.

primitives.name: onMouseEnter / onMouseLeave

// enter star 3 -> hover = 3
// leave the whole row -> hover = 0
primitives.note: Fire once when the pointer enters / leaves the element (they don't bubble from children like mouseover/mouseout). Put leave on the row, not each star, so moving between stars doesn't flicker.
